title: Arm A of Q nrch-turnover, negative: a slowly rising chemostat target makes the NRCH crystal's swimmers fatter, not more numerous (0 persistent splits, 2 seeds, T=9000)
summary: Chemostat crystal world (u=1.5e-3, phi0=-0.4, Dt=-0.3, 192^2) with phi_t ramped linearly from -0.4 to -0.3 between t=3000 and 8000 (world.py defaults). On seeds 0 and 1 the polar lattice forms by t~2400 and keeps its 25 and 20 swimmers to t=9000; the ramp adds material (occupancy 0.22 -> 0.27) by swelling every swimmer evenly (packs/RAMPs0/sheet.png t=4300-9000), with 3 and 2 splits in the whole run, 0 persistent. The swimmers themselves are the most persistent individuals of this class so far: 25 and 20 tracks alive >= 50% of the run, the longest ~8400 t, and up to 116 and 91 body lengths travelled. So in this lattice the feed sets swimmer size, not number: division needs a removal process (arm B: whole-body deaths) or a size threshold for fission, which a slow ramp to phi_t=-0.3 does not reach.

finding.operator: slowly ramped Model-A chemostat target on the NRCH swimmer lattice
finding.control: unramped lattice at the same u and phi0 (K5s0, K5s1 in 20261025T1054 and 20261025T1114)
finding.result: ramp -0.4 -> -0.3 over t=3000-8000: swimmers 25/20 constant, splits 3/2, persistent 0/0, occupancy 0.22 -> 0.27, longest tracks ~8400 t, 116/91 body lengths
